_comment: TinkerRocket design tokens for ANDROID. iOS is the design reference (decision 2026-07-30) and does NOT read this file: it calls SwiftUI's .green/.red/... and gets whatever the OS resolves, so it tracks Apple's retunes and Increase Contrast for free. Android cannot, so these are a frozen transcription of the iOS system colors and Android renders them instead of Material defaults. Being frozen, they go STALE: iOS 26 retuned seven of the nine palette entries (purple #AF52DE -> #CB30E0 is the largest). Values below captured 2026-08-12 by tools/capture_ios_palette.swift on the iOS 26.4 and 26.5 simulator runtimes (identical on both) -- re-run it after each major iOS release. Edit THIS file, then run tools/gen_design_tokens.py and commit the regenerated DesignTokens.swift / DesignTokens.kt (CI checks freshness). Platform-native things stay out of tokens by design: navigation mechanics, touch feedback, fonts (SF Pro cannot ship on Android; sizes/weights align via components).

roles._comment: Semantic color roles → palette entries. One role per user-facing meaning, so a screen never reaches for a raw palette color.

surfaces._comment: iOS system surfaces the app actually uses: cards are systemGray6, row chips inside cards are systemGray5, screens are systemBackground.

shape._comment: dp/pt. radiusButton is THE TinkerRocket radius (56 of 76 cornerRadius calls in the iOS app); radiusChip is the small one (flag chips, mini rows).

spacing._comment: dp/pt, from the iOS screens: .padding() = 16, top-screen VStack spacing = 20, in-row spacing = 12.
